docs.title: 🧬 Scientific Term Extraction Pipeline
docs.text: Production-ready pipeline for extracting biomedical terminology optimized for Common Data Model (CDM) implementation

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text: This advanced pipeline extracts high-quality biomedical terminology from scientific literature using 4 sciSpaCy models, multi-layer filtering, and semantic deduplication to achieve 98.4% accuracy in extracting clinically relevant terms.

docs.title: ✨ Key Features
docs.text:
• 🔬 Multi-Model NER: 4 specialized sciSpaCy models running in parallel
  • 🔍 4-Layer Filtering: Basic → Advanced → Biomedical → CDM optimization
  • 🔄 4-Strategy Deduplication: Exact → Fuzzy → Semantic → BioMistral Biomedical (NEW!)
  • 🏥 CDM Integration: Optimized for Common Data Model terminology
  • 💾 Multi-Format Output: JSON, CSV, SQLite with CDM schema
  • 🚀 Production Ready: FastAPI, Docker, monitoring stack

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text: The Configuration API provides comprehensive control over pipeline behavior, model selection, deduplication parameters, and safety settings. All configuration changes are validated before applying and can be persisted across sessions.

docs.title: Configuration Categories
docs.text:
• Pipeline Settings: Core extraction behavior and model selection
  • Deduplication: 4-layer deduplication parameters and thresholds
  • Quality Control: Minimum term requirements and quality scoring
  • Safety Features: Medical safety and critical term protection
  • Performance: Resource optimization and parallelization settings
  • Output: Format preferences and metadata inclusion

docs.title: PipelineConfig Structure
docs.text:
interface PipelineConfig {
  // Core pipeline settings
  pipeline: {
    models: {
      scispacy_models: string[]           // NER models to use
      semantic_model: "mini-lm" | "nomic" | "mpnet"
      ai_correction: {
        enabled: boolean
        model: string                     // BioMistral model path
        confidence_threshold: number      // 0.0-1.0
      }
      umls_mapping: {
        enabled: boolean
        api_key?: string
        version: string
      }
    }

    // 4-layer deduplication
    deduplication: {
      exact_enabled: boolean
      fuzzy_enabled: boolean
      fuzzy_threshold: number             // 0.0-1.0
      semantic_enabled: boolean
      semantic_threshold: number          // 0.0-1.0
      biomedical_enabled: boolean
      semantic_models: Record<string, string>
      default_semantic_model: string
    }

    // Quality requirements
    quality: {
      minimum_terms_per_file: number
      enable_quantity_safeguard: boolean
      strict_mode: boolean
      quality_threshold: number           // 0.0-1.0
    }

    // Safety settings
    safety: {
      medical_safety_enabled: boolean
      critical_terms_protection: boolean
      audit_trail_enabled: boolean
      phi_detection_enabled: boolean
    }

    // Performance settings
    performance: {
      parallel_processing: boolean
      max_workers: number
      batch_size: number
      gpu_enabled: boolean
      memory_optimization: boolean
    }

    // Output preferences
    output: {
      formats: ("json" | "csv" | "sqlite")[]
      include_ai_corrections: boolean
      include_biomedical_duplicates: boolean
      include_audit_trail: boolean
      output_directory?: string
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
# Get current configuration

     "http://localhost:8000/config"

import requests

def get_configuration(api_key=None):
    """Get current pipeline configuration"""
    headers = {}
    if api_key:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"

    response = requests.get("http://localhost:8000/config", headers=headers)

    if response.status_code == 200:
        data = response.json()
        return data["data"]["config"]
    else:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to get config: {response.text}")

docs.text:
# Update semantic model and thresholds
curl -X PUT "http://localhost:8000/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "pipeline": {
      "models": {
        "semantic_model": "mpnet"
      },
      "deduplication": {
        "fuzzy_threshold": 0.90
      }
    },
    "options": {
      "validate_models": true,
      "backup_current": true
    }
  }'

# Validate changes without applying
curl -X PUT "http://localhost:8000/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "pipeline": {
      "performance": {
        "max_workers": 16
      }
    },
    "options": {
      "validate_only": true
    }
  }'

import requests

def update_configuration(config_updates, api_key, validate_only=False):
    """Update pipeline configuration"""
    headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}",
        "Content-Type": "application/json"
    }

    payload = {
        "pipeline": config_updates,
        "options": {
            "validate_only": validate_only,
            "backup_current": True,
            "validate_models": True
        }
    }

    response = requests.put("http://localhost:8000/config",
                           json=payload, headers=headers)

    if response.status_code == 200:
        data = response.json()
        if validate_only:
            return data["data"]["validation"]
        else:
            return data["data"]["changes_applied"]
    else:
        error_data = response.json()
        raise Exception(f"Config update failed: {error_data['error']['message']}")

# Example: Enable UMLS mapping
config_updates = {
    "models": {
        "umls_mapping": {
            "enabled": True,
            "api_key": "your_umls_key"
        }
    }
}

try:
    changes = update_configuration(config_updates, "YOUR_API_KEY")
    print(f"Configuration updated: {changes}")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Update failed: {e}")

docs.text:
# Get all models
curl "http://localhost:8000/models"

# Get only scispacy models
curl "http://localhost:8000/models?type=scispacy"

# Get detailed information
curl "http://localhost:8000/models?detailed=true"

# Get only loaded models
curl "http://localhost:8000/models?status=loaded"

def get_models_info(model_type=None, status=None, detailed=False):
    """Get information about available models"""
    params = {}
    if model_type:
        params["type"] = model_type
    if status:
        params["status"] = status
    if detailed:
        params["detailed"] = "true"

    response = requests.get("http://localhost:8000/models", params=params)

    if response.status_code == 200:
        data = response.json()
        return data["data"]["models"]
    else:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to get models info: {response.text}")

# Get loaded semantic models
semantic_models = get_models_info(model_type="semantic", status="loaded")
for model in semantic_models:
    print(f"{model['name']}: {model['performance']['similarity_quality']}")

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text: The extraction endpoints provide the core functionality for processing scientific text and extracting biomedical terminology. These endpoints support various input methods, processing modes, and output formats to accommodate different use cases.

docs.title: Available Endpoints
docs.text:
• /extract - Asynchronous text extraction (recommended)
  • /extract/sync - Synchronous text extraction (immediate response)
  • /batch - Batch processing multiple texts
  • /upload - File upload and processing
  • /jobs/{job_id} - Retrieve job results
  • /files/{file_id} - Retrieve processed file results

docs.title: Processing Modes
docs.text: Mode Use Case Response Time Best For Async Large texts, production use Polling required Web applications, pipelines Sync Small texts, testing Immediate (up to 30s) APIs, real-time processing Batch Multiple documents Polling required Bulk processing, analysis Upload Document files Polling required File-based workflows

import requests

def analyze_text(text):
    response = requests.post(
        "http://localhost:8000/extract/sync",
        json={
            "text": text,
            "options": {
                "semantic_model": "mini-lm",
                "ai_correction_enabled": True
            }
        }
    )

    if response.status_code == 200:
        data = response.json()
        return {
            "terms": data["data"]["terms"],
            "quality_score": data["data"]["metadata"]["quality_score"],
            "processing_time": data["processing_time"]
        }
    else:
        return {"error": response.json()}

# Usage
result = analyze_text("Bacteroides fragilis produces short-chain fatty acids.")
print(f"Found {len(result['terms'])} terms with quality {result['quality_score']}")

docs.title: Use Case 2: Batch Processing Research Papers
docs.text:
import time
import requests

def process_research_papers(papers, callback_url=None):
    # Submit batch job
    response = requests.post(
        "http://localhost:8000/batch",
        json={
            "texts": papers,
            "options": {
                "semantic_model": "mpnet",
                "ai_correction_enabled": True,
                "umls_mapping_enabled": True,
                "domain": "research"
            },
            "callback_url": callback_url,
            "job_name": f"research_batch_{int(time.time())}"
        }
    )

    if response.status_code == 200:
        batch_data = response.json()
        return batch_data["data"]["batch_id"]
    else:
        raise Exception(f"Batch submission failed: {response.text}")

def wait_for_batch_completion(batch_id, max_wait=300):
    start_time = time.time()

    while time.time() - start_time < max_wait:
        # Check each job in the batch
        response = requests.get(f"http://localhost:8000/batches/{batch_id}")

        if response.status_code == 200:
            batch_data = response.json()

            if batch_data["data"]["status"] == "completed":
                return batch_data["data"]["results"]
            elif batch_data["data"]["status"] == "failed":
                raise Exception("Batch processing failed")

        time.sleep(5)

    raise TimeoutError("Batch processing timed out")

# Usage
papers = [
    "The gut microbiome composition varies between healthy individuals...",
    "Metagenomic sequencing reveals microbial diversity patterns...",
    "Antibiotic treatment significantly alters gut microbiota..."
]

batch_id = process_research_papers(papers)
results = wait_for_batch_completion(batch_id)

print(f"Processed {len(results['jobs'])} papers")
print(f"Total terms extracted: {sum(len(job['results']['terms']) for job in results['jobs'])}")

import requests
import time
from datetime import datetime

def monitor_system_health():
    """Comprehensive health monitoring script"""

    base_url = "http://localhost:8000"

    try:
        # Basic health check
        health_response = requests.get(f"{base_url}/health", timeout=5)
        basic_health = health_response.json()

        # Detailed health check
        detailed_response = requests.get(f"{base_url}/health/detailed", timeout=10)
        detailed_health = detailed_response.json()

        # System resources
        system_response = requests.get(f"{base_url}/health/system", timeout=5)
        system_health = system_response.json()

        # Queue status
        queue_response = requests.get(f"{base_url}/health/queue", timeout=5)
        queue_health = queue_response.json()

        # Compile health report
        report = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "overall_status": basic_health["status"],
            "uptime": basic_health["uptime"],
            "components": basic_health["checks"],
            "cpu_usage": system_health["cpu"]["usage_percent"],
            "memory_usage": system_health["memory"]["usage_percent"],
            "disk_usage": system_health["disk"]["usage_percent"],
            "queue_length": queue_health["queue_status"]["queued_jobs"],
            "active_jobs": queue_health["queue_status"]["active_jobs"],
            "processing_rate": queue_health["queue_performance"]["throughput_per_hour"],
            "success_rate": queue_health["queue_status"]["success_rate_percent"]
        }

        # Determine if alerts should be triggered
        alerts = []

        if report["cpu_usage"] > 80:
            alerts.append("High CPU usage detected")

        if report["memory_usage"] > 85:
            alerts.append("High memory usage detected")

        if report["disk_usage"] > 80:
            alerts.append("High disk usage detected")

        if report["queue_length"] > 50:
            alerts.append("High queue length detected")

        if report["success_rate"] < 95:
            alerts.append("Low success rate detected")

        report["alerts"] = alerts

        return report

    except requests.RequestException as e:
        return {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "status": "error",
            "error": str(e),
            "alerts": ["Health check failed"]
        }

def main():
    """Main monitoring loop"""

    while True:
        try:
            report = monitor_system_health()

            print(f"\n=== Health Report - {report['timestamp']} ===")
            print(f"Status: {report['overall_status'].upper()}")
            print(f"CPU: {report.get('cpu_usage', 'N/A')}%")
            print(f"Memory: {report.get('memory_usage', 'N/A')}%")
            print(f"Disk: {report.get('disk_usage', 'N/A')}%")
            print(f"Queue: {report.get('queue_length', 'N/A')} jobs")
            print(f"Success Rate: {report.get('success_rate', 'N/A')}%")

            if report.get('alerts'):
                print("\n⚠️ ALERTS:")
                for alert in report['alerts']:
                    print(f"  - {alert}")

            # Send alerts to monitoring system
            if report.get('alerts'):
                send_alerts_to_monitoring_system(report)

        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Monitoring error: {e}")

        time.sleep(60)  # Check every minute

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.text: The pipeline implements multiple layers of medical safety to ensure compliance with healthcare standards and preserve clinical specificity. Safety is not an afterthought – it's built into the core architecture.

docs.title: Safety Principles
docs.text:
1. Clinical Specificity First: Never collapse clinically distinct conditions
  2. Complete Provenance: Track every decision made by the pipeline
  3. Data Integrity: Verify transformations using cryptographic hashes

docs.title: Term Protection Logic
docs.text:
def _normalize_term(self, term: str, use_synonym_map: bool = True) -> str:
    """
    Safe term normalization with clinical specificity protection
    """
    original_term = term.strip()

    # BLOCK 1: Never normalize critical clinical terms
    if original_term in CRITICAL_CLINICAL_TERMS:
        return original_term  # Preserve exact terminology

    # BLOCK 2: Expand abbreviations (preserves specificity)
    if original_term.lower() in ABBREVIATION_EXPANSION:
        expanded = ABBREVIATION_EXPANSION[original_term.lower()]
        # Only expand if it doesn't conflict with clinical specificity
        if expanded not in CRITICAL_CLINICAL_TERMS:
            original_term = expanded

    # BLOCK 3: Apply only safe synonym mappings
    if use_synonym_map:
        # Only normalize truly equivalent terms
        if original_term in SAFE_SYNONYM_MAP:
            candidate = SAFE_SYNONYM_MAP[original_term]
            # Final safety check
            if candidate not in CRITICAL_CLINICAL_TERMS:
                return candidate
            else:
                return original_term  # Safety over normalization

    return original_term

def _should_trigger_human_review(self, term_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    """Determine if term requires human medical review"""

    term = term_data.get('term', '').lower()

    review_triggers = [
        term in CRITICAL_CLINICAL_TERMS,
        'drug' in term and 'resistance' in term,  # Antibiotic resistance
        'genetic' in term and 'mutation' in term,  # Genetic mutations
        'death' in term or 'mortality' in term,  # Mortality data
        term_data.get('confidence', 1.0) < 0.5,  # Low confidence
    ]

    return any(review_triggers)

def verify_transformation_integrity(self, original_data: Dict, transformed_data: Dict) -> bool:
    """Verify that data transformation maintained integrity"""

    # Generate hash of original data
    original_hash = hashlib.sha256(
        json.dumps(original_data, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
    ).hexdigest()

    # Compare with stored input hash
    stored_input_hash = transformed_data.get('integrity_hash', '')

class MedicalReviewSystem:
    """System for medical professional review of pipeline decisions"""

    def flag_for_review(self, terms: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Flag terms requiring medical review"""
        flagged_terms = []

        for term_data in terms:
            if self._should_trigger_human_review(term_data):
                term_data['medical_review_required'] = True
                term_data['review_status'] = 'pending'
                flagged_terms.append(term_data)

        return flagged_terms

    def create_review_batch(self, flagged_terms: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
        """Create review batch for medical professionals"""
        review_file = f"medical_review_batch_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}.csv"

        with open(review_file, 'w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            fieldnames = ['term', 'context', 'confidence', 'reason_for_review', 'status']
            writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)
            writer.writeheader()

            for term_data in flagged_terms:
                writer.writerow({
                    'term': term_data.get('term', ''),
                    'context': term_data.get('context', ''),
                    'confidence': term_data.get('confidence', 0.0),
                    'reason_for_review': self._get_review_reason(term_data),
                    'status': term_data.get('review_status', 'pending')
                })

        return review_file

docs.title: 4-Layer Biomedical Deduplication
docs.text: The pipeline features an advanced 4-layer deduplication system that progressively removes duplicates at different levels of semantic understanding.

docs.title: Layer 1: Exact Deduplication
docs.text:
• Purpose: Remove identical terms
  • Method: String normalization and exact matching
  • Configuration: Always enabled
  • Performance: Very fast, removes obvious duplicates

docs.title: Layer 2: Fuzzy Deduplication
docs.text:
• Purpose: Remove similar terms with minor variations
  • Method: RapidFuzz string similarity
  • Threshold: 85% (configurable)
  • Examples: DNA extraction vs DNA extractions

docs.title: Layer 3: Semantic Deduplication
docs.text:
• Purpose: Remove semantically equivalent terms
  • Method: Sentence-transformer embeddings with cosine similarity
  • Models: Mini-LM, Nomic v1.5, MPNet
  • Threshold: 90% (configurable)
  • Examples: gut microbiota vs intestinal microflora

docs.title: Layer 4: BioMistral Biomedical Deduplication ⭐ NEW
docs.text:
• Purpose: Context-aware biomedical duplicate detection
  • Method: BioMistral/BioPubMedBERT classification with domain-specific prompts
  • Context: Microbiome, biomedical, clinical, genomics
  • Confidence: High-confidence duplicate detection with reasoning

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Semantic Grouping: Terms are first grouped by semantic similarity
  2. Biomedical Classification: Each term pair is evaluated by BioMistral for biomedical equivalence
  3. Context-Aware Prompts: Specialized prompts for different biomedical domains
  4. Duplicate Clustering: Advanced clustering to find duplicate groups
  5. Reasoning Storage: Detailed reasoning for each duplicate decision
